previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, type 2 diabetes, hypertension, coronary artery disease, and recent gout, was admitted with persistent left knee pain and fatigue. Initial evaluation revealed no signs of gout or infection in the knee, but a left peroneal vein DVT was identified on Doppler ultrasound. He also had fluid overload with pulmonary edema, likely exacerbated by recent prednisone use, which improved with IV furosemide and transition to oral torsemide. A chest X-ray incidentally showed lower lobe pneumonia, for which he completed a five-day course of antibiotics. His kidney function, initially impaired with a creatinine of 2.9, improved to 2.2 by discharge. Warfarin was initiated for DVT, with INR monitored closely. GERD symptoms were managed by increasing pantoprazole to twice daily. He was discharged home on warfarin, torsemide, adjusted doses of home medications, and follow-up plans including INR monitoring and transplant nephrology visit.
